title: Wholesale portal report data cache — local verification

environment.working_tree: Existing unrelated local changes retained. Git HEAD alone does not identify measured code; source fingerprints below do.
environment.production: No deployment, schema change, production configuration change, or live financial test mutation. Timing improvements below are local only.

cached_sources: Scoped commerce orders and complete sibling order items
Historical production runs, with a separate key for each recent-order fallback product set
Sales-rep dropdown display rows only when no rep selection needs fresh validation
uncached: Current center assignments and sales-rep membership/scope
implementation.isolation: Authenticated RLS reads retained. Keys include datasource URL, actor, current access map and role/profile flags, normalized effective scope, source query identity, exact database filters, and local mutation generation. Lifetime, comparison period and filtered recent orders cannot collide. Display-only product/customer filters recompute totals from shared rows.
implementation.freshness: 30-second maximum cached-read age measured from query start. A timestamped envelope and foreground wait override Next's stale-while-revalidate behavior. The same refresh promise is reused; expired data is never returned as an error fallback. Stable keys avoid a new persistent entry every time window.
implementation.invalidation: Successful PostgREST writes and mutating RPCs through authenticated server, service-role, and route clients expire one shared report-data tag. This conservatively covers order, inventory, production, payroll, catalog, assignment, recurring cron, portal, Shopify, and QuickBooks changes. GET/HEAD, auth/storage endpoints, read RPCs and touch_profile_last_seen do not invalidate.
implementation.local_compatibility: A process-global generation survives HMR and prevents repeated local writes or an older local in-flight fill from reusing invalidated entries; managed tag invalidation remains in place for other instances.
implementation.manual_refresh: Authorized Refresh data server action clears report data and refreshes the route. Report-tab prefetch is disabled; each server visit checks current access before cached data.

freshness_tradeoffs: An already-open report is a snapshot and does not auto-refresh. Navigate or use Refresh data to see changes.

Normal application writes invalidate affected cached sources conservatively on the next server visit. External SQL and raw-client repair scripts bypass this hook; subsequent visits can reuse data for at most 30 seconds.

This is not a transactional cross-query snapshot. A concurrent read/write race across server instances or a distributed invalidation failure can also leave cached data reusable within the same 30-second bound. Failed invalidation logs a static diagnostic while preserving committed database-write success.
Current authorization is checked afresh; the freshness allowance never applies to profile status, permissions, or resolved scope.

measurement_method.account: Existing authenticated owner session in Codex in-app browser
measurement_method.metric: Existing browser marker: captured link click/document navigation to React commit effect. Server phases are timed separately; overlapping spans must not be added.
measurement_method.main_sequence: Overview first visit with five misses; reload; first Centers visit and reload sharing all five sources; Recent Order GPM first visit (three hits, one miss) and reload; three Overview → Centers → Recent cycles.
measurement_method.first_visit_caveat: First visits are per tab, not guaranteed cold processes or networks. Centers shares Overview's data immediately. Reload timings include document/layout work and can hit the data cache.
measurement_method.verification_sequence: After 36.8 seconds since the last repeat, Overview missed all five sources and waited for fresh queries; Centers then hit all five. Two consecutive Refresh data actions each missed all five, followed by related-tab hits. Final financial output compared on four reports.
measurement_method.controls: Dashboard and Orders retained their original uncached query paths and were measured separately before the final timestamp-envelope revision. The common Supabase client wrappers were already final.
limitations: Three repeat observations per page, not a load test or percentile SLO.
Network/auth variance remains: Recent had one 436ms hit dominated by 367ms authentication. Cold Overview was 2434ms; later expiry refill was 1427ms.
Dashboard/Orders repeat medians were slower than the previous run; this cache makes no improvement claim for them.
No production cache propagation or multi-instance load test was performed.

findings: Warm report commerce reads now take roughly 1–2ms instead of repeated 0.4–1.0s database work.
Warm main-data phases take about 1.4–2.5ms. Authentication at roughly 113–153ms usually dominates the remaining server time.
First loads still incur database work. Full document reloads also retain shared layout/auth costs.
Overview/Centers retain 230 orders, 303 items and 381 historical production runs; Recent retains 10 orders/16 complete lines, with no production fetch needed for these fully snapshotted orders.

coverage: Access revocation before warm reads; actor/role/scope/datasource/filter isolation
Fresh selected-rep validation and fail-closed scope errors
Preload → successful order/inventory/production/payroll write → changed financial result
Two successive invalidations/refills, client wiring and neutral/failed requests
Strict age expiry, no stale-on-error fallback, one refresh per read, bounded keys across TTL renewals
Historical COGS fallbacks, pagination completeness, comparison/lifetime metrics, complete financial allocations
correctness.browser_comparison: Exact visible main-content text on Overview, Centers, Recent Order GPM, Sales matches the pre-cache version after excluding only the new Refresh data control/copy and blank lines.
correctness.live_mutations: Only the local cache refresh action was invoked. Database mutation correctness uses mocked network/fixtures, not modifications to real orders or payroll.
